title: Beyond Gluten-Free: A Comprehensive Assessment of Dietary Intake and Quality in Adults with Celiac Disease in Greece
content: Background/Objectives: Nutritional imbalances in the context of gluten-free diet (GFD) among individuals with celiac disease (CeD) remains a subject of ongoing research. The aim of the present study was to provide the first comprehensive dietary assessment of adults with CeD in Greece. Methods: Adults with biopsy-confirmed CeD on GFD were recruited from general hospitals of the Attica region. Dietary intake was assessed by three nonconsecutive 24-hour recalls, and analyzed at the macronutrient, food-group, and NOVA classification intake levels. Additional assessment included adherence to GFD, the Mediterranean diet (MD), and anthropometric measurements. Results: The sample consisted of 111 individuals (71.2% females), with a median age of 42 years. Lipids contributed 44.5% (± 7.6) of total energy intake, while protein intake was adequate for nearly the entire cohort. Intakes of saturated fatty acids and sugars exceeded, whereas fiber intake fell below, the reference values in more than 80% of participants. Ultra-processed (NOVA 4) foods accounted for 18% (10.1, 26.4) of total energy intake, while ultra-processed cereals represented almost half of all NOVA 4 portions. Notably, half of bread consumers consumed exclusively NOVA 4 options. Several food groups contained no ultra-processed items. Adherence to the MD was moderate in 87% of participants. Conclusions: Our cohort exhibited a sub-optimal dietary pattern high in fat, low in fiber, and over-reliant on animal protein. Nutritional counseling to integrate fiber-rich grains and pulses, while mitigating major UPF sources, is essential to improve the overall dietary quality.
